named_public_imports_and_scope: Two explicit public imports are used: (I) Yang, Leung and Tang, arXiv:1603.03534v1, https://arxiv.org/html/1603.03534v1, Corollary 3.6, every 3x3 PPT state has Schmidt number <=2; (II) Chen and Djokovic, arXiv:1301.2372v1, https://arxiv.org/html/1301.2372v1, Proposition 5(i), every bipartite PPT entangled state has rank strictly greater than the larger local rank. These imports are not independently re-proved here. All statements depending on them are conditional on the imports. The Schur-lifting and extreme-state arguments below are independently written. No held episode, selected-parameter episode, Johnston–Lovitz construction, fixed-KG pair, or symplectic-family assumption is used.
claim: If any 4x4 PPT state has Schmidt number >=3, there exists an extreme normalized PPT state rho_* with Schmidt number >=3 whose local ranks are either (3,4), (4,3), or (4,4). Under imports I-II its birank r=rank(rho_*), s=rank(rho_*^Gamma) satisfies r,s>=5; for the (3,4)/(4,3) branch, r^2+s^2<=145, 5<=r,s<=10 and min(r,s)<=8; for the full-local (4,4) branch, r^2+s^2<=257, 5<=r,s<=15 and min(r,s)<=11. In the full-local branch every rank-three local projection on either side yields a PPT entangled state of full local ranks (3,4) or (4,3), and both it and its partial transpose have rank at least 5. Consequently, if r=5 then range(rho_*) is completely entangled, and if s=5 then range(rho_*^Gamma) is completely entangled. These are necessary conditions, not a construction or a 4x4 no-go.
general_schur_lift_lemma: For any bipartite PSD rho, any local orthogonal projection P of codimension t, and sigma=(P tensor I)rho(P tensor I), SN(rho)<=SN(sigma)+t, with SN(0)=0. Proof: relative to P and I-P write rho=[[A,B],[B^*,D]], A=sigma. If A=0 then B=0 by PSD and rho is supported on the t-dimensional deleted factor. Otherwise take a Schmidt-rank-s decomposition A=VV^*=sum_i[v_i], s=SN(A). PSD implies range(B) subset range(A) and D-B^*A^dagger B>=0. Put C=B^* A^dagger V. Then V C^*=B and C C^*=B^* A^dagger B, so rho=sum_i[v_i direct_sum c_i]+diag(0,D-B^*A^dagger B). Every v_i direct_sum c_i has Schmidt rank <=s+t, because c_i is supported on the deleted t-dimensional factor; the PSD remainder is supported there and has Schmidt number <=t. Thus the bound is constructive. Local compression never increases Schmidt number, giving SN(sigma)<=SN(rho)<=SN(sigma)+t.
extreme_selection_and_local_ranks: Given any target rho, compact convex separation from the normalized Schmidt-number<=2 set gives a 2-block-positive W with Tr(W rho)<0. Minimize this linear functional over the compact normalized PPT set and take an extreme minimizer; it is an extreme PPT state with Schmidt number >=3. Its local ranks are at least 3, since Schmidt number never exceeds either local rank. Import I excludes (3,3), so the local ranks are among (3,4),(4,3),(4,4). Partial transpose preserves local ranks, and a PPT state is separable iff its partial transpose is separable. Hence rho_* and rho_*^Gamma are PPT entangled; import II yields r,s>max(local ranks)=4.
extreme_birank_dimension: On the local support of dimensions m,n, let P_R and Q_R be the support projections of rho_* and rho_*^Gamma. The real subspaces {H=P_R H P_R} and {H^Gamma=Q_R H^Gamma Q_R} of Herm(mn) have dimensions r^2 and s^2, hence their intersection has dimension at least r^2+s^2-(mn)^2. An independent traceless element of the intersection could be added/subtracted by a sufficiently small real multiple while keeping both operators PSD on their supports, contradicting extremality. Thus r^2+s^2<=(mn)^2+1. With r,s>=5, the (3,4) or (4,3) case gives r,s<=10 and min<=8; the (4,4) case gives r,s<=15 and min<=11.
extreme_edge_marginal_lemma: Let rho be an extreme entangled PPT state whose two local marginals are full rank. Then every codimension-one projection on either local system leaves the OTHER marginal full rank. For an Alice projection P=I-[a], suppose the Bob marginal of (P tensor I)rho(P tensor I) has nonzero kernel b. PSD gives rho|x,b>=0 for every x perpendicular to a; PPT likewise gives rho^Gamma|x,conjugate(b)>=0. The full Bob marginal gives <a,b|rho|a,b>>0. For every x perpendicular to a and c, <x,c|rho|a,b>=<x,conjugate(b)|rho^Gamma|a,conjugate(c)>=0, so rho|a,b>=|a> tensor v with v nonzero. The analogous identity gives rho^Gamma|a,conjugate(b)>=|a> tensor conjugate(v). Thus |a,v> lies in range(rho) and |a,conjugate(v)> lies in range(rho^Gamma). A sufficiently small positive multiple of the product projector [a tensor v] can be subtracted while preserving both PSD conditions, contradicting extremality of entangled rho. The Bob-side assertion follows by swapping subsystems.
full_local_cut_consequences: If rho_* has full 4x4 local ranks, every Alice rank-three cut has local ranks (3,4): the retained Alice marginal is positive definite on its three-space and the edge-marginal lemma gives the full Bob marginal. The Schur-lift lemma forces its Schmidt number >=2, so it is PPT entangled. Its partial transpose is also PPT entangled with the same local ranks. Import II therefore gives rank >=5 for both. The same holds for every Bob rank-three cut with local ranks (4,3). Because rank((P tensor I)rho_*(P tensor I))=r-dim(range(rho_*) intersect (span(a) tensor C^4)), every such fiber intersection has dimension <=r-5; the corresponding statement holds for rho_*^Gamma and for Bob fibers, with conjugated Bob projections where appropriate. If r=5 all these intersections vanish, so range(rho_*) has no product vector; if s=5 the same holds for range(rho_*^Gamma).
direct_pruning_rule: Independently of the two public imports and independently of PPT, if a 4x4 PSD candidate has even one rank-three local projection that is separable, the explicit Schur-lift lemma constructs an SN<=2 decomposition of the original state. Conversely a valid SN>=3 candidate must have every such projection entangled. This is a necessary condition only, not a sufficient criterion for SN>=3.
